editorial.headline: Chocolate Manufacturing With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10732 covers chocolate products, chocolate-based sweets, spreads, fillings, and chocolate drinks, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10732 is a manufacturing code for chocolate in several forms.** The record places it around the making of compound chocolate, couverture chocolate, imitation chocolate, white chocolate, and chocolate confectionery. It also includes chocolate-based spreads and fillings, and it reaches into chocolate drinks when they are made in powder or liquid form. In plain English, this is not a retail shelf category or a cafe concept; it is the activity of producing chocolate and chocolate-derived products.

That breadth matters because the code is not limited to one premium or mass-market expression of chocolate. The slim record names both couverture and imitation chocolate, which gives the activity a practical manufacturing range, from ingredients used in further preparation to finished sweets and drink bases. The common thread is the chocolate basis of the output. A founder reading this code should therefore focus on whether the planned activity is the making of those chocolate goods, spreads, fillings, or drinks, rather than on how the product will later be branded, sold, or consumed.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. KBLI 10732 is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the activity is not framed, in this slim record, as only a large industrial category or only a small producer category. It can describe a micro operation, a small or medium manufacturer, or a large-scale manufacturer, as long as the underlying activity remains the manufacture of the chocolate products described in the scope. The scale field is important here because it tells the founder that the activity itself can sit across the full range named in the record.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clear. Nationally, the activity's PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to a 100% ceiling. In practical editorial terms, the national record treats this chocolate manufacturing activity as open to foreign ownership up to the full ceiling stated in the data. Bali does not add a separate percentage in the record, and it should not be read as doing so. The Bali-side status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium”. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently; this code is not marked as blocked by that rule. The honest reading is therefore simple: nationally, the code is open up to 100% foreign ownership, and in Bali the slim record does not mark it as blocked for PMA registration.
